prompts.name: Human Hours
prompts.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, purposeful spacing. Use case ui-mockup. Create ONE independent premium marketing website visual direction for WaitListFit, waitlistfit.com, US-first specialty clinic capacity research concept. Target canvas 1440px wide by 1920px tall, representing a desktop website opening and its first scroll story chapter, no browser chrome, no device frames, not a brand guideline poster. Dates anchored to 16 October 2026; the synthetic case is Tuesday 13 October 2026, cancellation 10:30–11:00, 30 minutes. Audience specialty-practice COO, access director, scheduling manager. Primary action "Request a replay"; secondary "Explore the demo". Required main headline exactly "Make specialty appointment capacity visible before a scheduler fills the slot." Set it beautifully with intentional line breaks. Brief subcopy about a proposed read-only queue with scheduler approval. Navigation may show Products, How it works, Pilot & pricing. Logo says WaitListFit with an original tasteful small mark; existing W is optional, previous identity is NOT approved and may be reinterpreted.
First story chapter: "Tuesday. One cancellation. Three candidates." Show a concise concrete scene with clinician, room, visit length, equipment, authorization, interpreter and transport constraints. Candidate A room mismatch, Candidate B interpreter unavailable, Candidate C awaiting scheduler review. Synthetic fictional IDs only. Clearly visible "CONCEPT PREVIEW" and "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA". Never show automatically booked, sent, revenue, customer logos, testimonials, ROI, compliance badges, invented integrations or clinical advice. No PHI, no medical diagnosis.
Only hero plus one or two connected narrative moments, not all five modules stuffed into one image. The complete future site has five modules but no need to invent or display them all in this direction image. Typography no more than two complementary families, readable interface labels, restrained spacing. Avoid card grids, cards inside cards, generic AI orbs, robots, flat default SaaS template, oversized default centered app screenshot.
Attached references 1–2 are real frames of Dawn supplied in a recording: use ONLY the sense of continuous atmosphere, gradient transition and narrative pacing, never copy its logo, copy, portraits or claims. Attached reference 3 is our previous WaitListFit brand study: product/copy grounding only; USER NOW WANTS VERY DIFFERENT VISUAL DIRECTIONS, so do not reuse its green/cream rounded-card split layout. This is a new visual concept, not an edit of those images. Do not include direction labels or option numbers in the website artwork.
Direction name: Human Hours. A photographic, cinematic, warm editorial design that feels commissioned by a world-class independent studio. Dominant palette pale peach #F5E8DC, warm aubergine #492B3A, terracotta #C56A48, soft sunlight ivory. Beautiful contemporary serif display (Canela-like) with modest clean sans labels. Start with a full-bleed photographic architectural hero, a softly sunlit contemporary clinic reception corridor, no people/patients and no visible medical logos or signage. Cream plaster, warm timber, translucent glass, linen-like daylight; mature and real, not stock corporate. Integrate generous left-aligned editorial headline in a naturally quiet light portion of the image; photo's curved architecture on the right visually creates the time interval. A very thin aubergine clinic-day line travels organically across the space, annotated 10:30 and 11:00, becoming the continuous line in the section below.
Use a refined narrow horizontal navigation, wordmark top-left, plum pill CTA top-right. Hero is expansive and asymmetric, not split into two cards. The lower 40% gradually washes from photographic warm light to a flat blush-paper editorial chapter; display the three candidate rationales as elegant typographic rows along a continuous route, with fine rules and no dashboard box. Elegant contrast, precise proportions, airy spacing, tangible photography as the dominant visual difference. This should feel like a premium hospitality/editorial studio applying craft to healthcare operations, without pretending to be a consumer wellness site. One coherent original composition with real content, not a collage.

Direction name: Capacity Index. Radically different from photographic/editorial warm brands: a Swiss international-style operational journal with striking typographic hierarchy, disciplined asymmetrical grid, white #FAFAF7, ink #181B1A, vivid restrained vermilion #E94A32. No photography, no gradients, no serif typography, no rounded hero cards, no green/cream style. Sophisticated light-first design with giant beautifully kerned modern grotesk typography (Neue Haas / Helvetica Now-like), medium weights, small precise monospaced data labels as second family. Lots of white space, razor-thin grid rules, a strong orange-red flat rectangular CTA.
Composition: top narrow black wordmark and minimal nav. Hero headline sits on left in a forceful 6-column editorial block. To the right a huge precisely typeset "30" with tiny MINUTES and a scale of time ticks; this is a measured interval, not an outcome metric. Below the headline one concise subline "A proposed read-only queue. Every next step belongs to the scheduler." and CTA. The 30-minute interval becomes a wide full-bleed horizontal resource score across the page's middle, with room, interpreter, equipment rows and time ticks like a beautifully designed transit map, not a generic weekly calendar. At the lower page, contrast switches to black with white text for a powerful inspection chapter, still connected by a red vertical rule from the hero. Layout uses numbered typographic rows A/B/C for candidates with explicit room mismatch, interpreter unavailable, awaiting scheduler review. Put DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA near the map and list. Every decorative element must relate to time, constraint or evidence. Brand tone sharp, intelligent, confident, controlled. No portraits, no pebble objects, no soft blobs, no huge boxes. Never use phrase "clinical fit" or invent clinical eligibility; labels are recorded operational constraints only. No testimonials or decorative quotation statements. Exact target 1440 x 1920 desktop canvas; original polished art direction, not a wireframe.

Direction name: Threadwork. An entirely different, highly crafted contemporary creative-studio identity: light pearl-lavender #F1EFF6, deep ink-plum #302941, restrained pale citron #D8E88A, chalk white. No photography, no brown/green editorial styling, no Swiss black/red layout, no giant number. Use a graceful rounded geometric sans-serif for headlines (Sora-like, medium NOT super heavy) and a small precise UI sans. Center the hero composition asymmetrically around a breathtaking bespoke sculptural artwork of FOUR very thin matte folded-paper ribbons arranged as labeled resource tracks through the page. These are clearly meaningful scheduling lanes, not generic AI blobs or floating toys. One white ribbon says clinician, another room, one interpreter, another equipment in tiny tasteful lettering. Each ribbon has a 30-minute cutout/interval. The tracks sweep in perspective from the lower-left across to the upper-right and almost line up at a single citron interval. Long soft contact shadows and tactile paper edge detail, subtle ambient light, highly art-directed tangible materials. Avoid glossy 3D, glassmorphism and sci-fi networks.
Create a spacious mostly light continuous webpage. Upper nav slim rounded wordmark WaitListFit, minimal links. Headline occupies upper center-left with plenty of breathing room, no headline card. CTA is ink-plum rounded rectangular. Large sculptural lanes occupy center/right and flow DOWN across the section boundary into a flat crisp candidate-review scene below. Small chapter markers in the left gutter create a scrollytelling feel. Lower chapter should have a plum background occupying only lower quarter, containing a sophisticated horizontal A/B/C candidate strip, separated by hairlines rather than separate cards. Explicit "Room mismatch", "Interpreter unavailable", "Awaiting scheduler review". Header of lower chapter "Tuesday. One cancellation. Three candidates." Distinctive editorial art direction where meaningful tactile resource ribbons become real labeled UI. The visual transition is the story: a proposed fit, then evidence, then a human decision. Bold enough to be memorable, mature enough for specialty practice leaders.
Keep case IDs fictional and all constraints operational. No term clinical fit, no patient eligibility judgment, no testimonials or fake facts. Show "CONCEPT PREVIEW" beside hero and "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA" beside lower case. No sign-in to imply an active product. Do not fill whitespace with extra slogans or badges. Crisp legible text, polished spacing, one cohesive desktop 1440x1920 image, no multi-option collage.
